title: Over $60 billion in capex required to meet 2040 lithium demand
gist: Benchmark estimates lithium operating supply must grow from 1.7 million tonnes LCE today to more than 4.7 million tonnes LCE by 2040, requiring roughly $64 billion of capex, with supply-side risk (permitting, financing, geopolitics) now seen as the greater uncertainty than demand, which is being pulled up by a second surprisingly strong year of BESS growth; unconventional sources like DLE are set to double their share of production to 40% by 2040.

insights.claim: Operating lithium supply needs to expand by more than 3 million tonnes LCE from today's level to meet Benchmark's 2040 base-case demand forecast.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Defines the scale of new mine and processing capacity the industry must bring online over the next 14 years, a key sizing input for capital allocation to lithium developers.
insights.quote: Operating lithium supply will need to expand by over three million tonnes LCE to meet expected 2040 base demand

insights.claim: Closing the lithium supply gap to 2040 is forecast to require approximately $64 billion in capital spending, according to Benchmark's Capex Briefing.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A concrete capex figure investors can use to size the financing opportunity across miners, project developers, and capital providers in the lithium value chain through 2040.
insights.quote: It is a gap that is forecast to require USD ~$64 billion in capital spending to close

insights.claim: Today's operating lithium supply stands at roughly 1.7 million tonnes LCE, versus a 2040 base-case demand level implied to be above 4.7 million tonnes LCE.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Gives investors the current supply baseline against which to measure whether announced project pipelines are on track to close the gap.
insights.quote: Operating supply in 2026 sits at 1.7 million tonnes LCE today

themes.theme: Demand Side: EV Plus a BESS Surprise

insights.claim: Benchmark's base demand view has lithium demand expanding at a 7.3% compound annual growth rate through 2040, driven by sustained EV adoption and rising battery energy storage system (BESS) deployment.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A 7.3% CAGR anchors long-run lithium demand models used to underwrite mine financing and offtake agreements.
insights.quote: demand for the mineral continues to expand at 7.3% CAGR under Benchmark's base demand view

insights.claim: BESS deployment is having a second consecutive year of growth that has surprised to the upside, surpassing Benchmark's initial estimates, per lithium analyst Federico Gay.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Repeated upside surprises in BESS demand suggest analysts across the industry may still be underestimating stationary storage as a lithium demand driver, a potential source of forecast upgrades and tighter markets than currently modeled.
insights.quote: demand, particularly BESS, is having a second surprising year of growth, which surpassed our initial estimates

themes.theme: Supply, Not Demand, Is the Bigger Swing Factor

insights.claim: Federico Gay contends the supply side, not demand, is the greater source of uncertainty for the lithium market, with permitting delays, financing constraints and geopolitical risks skewing supply risk to the downside.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Runs counter to demand-centric narratives around EV slowdowns; investors should track project permitting and financing news flow, not just EV sales data, as the leading indicator for lithium tightness.
insights.quote: the supply side does remain the greater source of uncertainty. Permitting delays, financing constraints and geopolitical risks suggest supply risk is skewed to the downside

insights.claim: Benchmark expects the lithium market to tighten in the medium term while maintaining a strong long-term growth trend, though a more challenging macroeconomic environment or reduced policy support could keep the market looser than the base case.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Gives investors an explicit bull/bear scenario framework: base case is tightening, with macro/policy deterioration as the key downside risk to monitor.

themes.theme: Rise of DLE and Unconventional Lithium Sources

insights.claim: Roughly 80% of current global lithium production comes from conventional sources, primarily spodumene hard-rock mines and brine evaporation.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Establishes the baseline production mix against which the shift toward DLE and sedimentary sources should be measured.
insights.quote: roughly 80% of total lithium production is produced from conventional sources, mainly spodumene mines and brines via evaporation

insights.claim: Direct lithium extraction (DLE), sedimentary, and mica sources are forecast to double their combined share of global lithium production to 40% by 2040, from roughly 20% today.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Signals a structural shift in the lithium supply mix that investors should track via DLE technology providers and project developers as a distinct, higher-growth sub-sector within lithium mining.
insights.quote: those sources, together with mica sources, will double their combined share of production to 40% by 2040

insights.claim: The new mines required to close the 2040 supply gap are geologically and technically more complex than legacy assets, and DLE and sedimentary projects carry higher capital requirements per tonne than conventional mines as a result.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Explains why the $64B capex figure is front-loaded toward complex, capital-intensive projects, implying DLE developers will need larger financing rounds and may face longer lead times to reach positive returns.
insights.quote: a significant share of the mines that need to be developed to bridge the supply gap are more complex, both geologically and technically, and that complexity carries a cost
